summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his teaching on the book of Salah, focusing on the Islamic ruling regarding the Adhan (call to prayer). Using a hadith from Sahih Bukhari, he explains the story of Abdullah ibn Abbas advising a shepherd to make the Adhan loudly while herding sheep in the wilderness, as it will be witnessed by jinn and humans on the Day of Judgment. Sh. Ali Mashhour then elaborates on the Islamic concept of Fard Kifayah (collective obligation) versus Fard Ayn (individual obligation), clarifying that the Adhan is a Fard Kifayah—if one person makes it, others are relieved of the obligation, but if no one makes it, all are held responsible. He provides practical examples and explains that when praying in an area where the Adhan has already been called, one only needs to make the Iqamah (second call), but when alone or in an area where no Adhan has been made, one must make both the Adhan and Iqamah before prayer.
